title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

reading.body:
This is an alleged misuse of law enforcement systems by someone with authorised access to them. The systems named are a Flock camera network, a tag reader system, and the Georgia Crime Information Center database, all of which are built to be queried by officers for official purposes. The alleged failure is not that the technology malfunctioned but that a legitimate user turned it to a personal end, using location and identity data to track a woman without her consent. The point of failure sits at the access layer, where the system trusts the operator's stated reason for a query.

Catching this kind of misuse is difficult because the queries themselves look ordinary. Detection would depend on audit trails of who searched whom and when, on comparing those searches against case assignments, and on someone reviewing the pattern rather than the individual lookup. A system that logs queries but never reconciles them against legitimate need will not surface this on its own.

The reporting describes an indictment and an allegation, not a finding of guilt. Rozar has been released on bond, and the charges against him have not been adjudicated. Whether the searches occurred as described, and for the reasons alleged, is not established by the reporting summarised here.

reports.title: Alleged victim speaks out after former Coffee Co. deputy accused of tracking her is released on bond

summary:
A former Coffee County sheriff's deputy, Chris Ashley Rozar, 49, has been released on bond after a grand jury indicted him on eight counts, including four counts of violating his oath, two counts of computer invasion of privacy, one count of prohibited use of captured license plate data, and one count of stalking. Prosecutors allege that between April 10 and May 1, 2024, Rozar misused the sheriff's office Flock camera system, tag reader system, and the Georgia Crime Information Center database for personal reasons, including tracking and surveilling a woman without her consent. The GBI investigated, and Rozar was terminated when the investigation began.

The woman at the center of the case spoke anonymously to WALB, saying she hopes her story encourages other women to report abuse. She said she waited two years for the investigation to finish and wants to move forward. Rozar was arrested on May 5 and released on bond the same day. He is scheduled for arraignment on May 27 in Coffee County Superior Court.
